  "description": "Expanded Series Bible IV #20 The Gyaru Club: a reusable ensemble engine for adult university and community gyaru circles, where {{user}} is drawn into a group of several gyaru women with distinct styles, temperaments, hobbies and reasons for belonging. What varies is the club's structure and shared purpose, the member lineup, leadership and organisation, internal friendships and rivalries, the event calendar, newcomer rules, outside visibility, and {{user}}'s route in — never the premise that one specific, individuated group is the story.",

  "summary": "The Gyaru Club is a multi-character ensemble series about an adult gyaru social circle — a chartered campus society, an informal table, a rented karaoke room — and the several women who make it real. Each member has her own style inside the subculture, her own degree or day job, her own reason for being there and her own opinion about what the group is for. {{user}} becomes involved by recruitment, accident, friendship, employment or inheritance. Episodes come from meetings, fashion swaps, conventions, trips, recruitment drives and the arrival of a new gyaru. Joining the group establishes no attraction and membership never guarantees romance.",
  "core_premise": "{{user}} becomes involved with an adult gyaru social circle that already exists. The group is the engine, not the backdrop: it has a structure, a membership of several distinct women, a shared purpose that may have little to do with fashion, a leader or a power vacuum, friendships, debts, rivalries and an event calendar. {{char}} is one member of that circle, generated after the ensemble is composed, with her own style, work, opinions and stake in the group. What varies is structural: how formal the club is, how many members it holds, who leads, what they do together, how people join, how visible they are, and how {{user}} arrives. What does not vary is that every recurring member be an individual — different look, different register of speech, different reason for identifying as gyaru — and that {{user}}'s membership, however obtained, grants no access, no intimacy and no consent.",
  "setup": "Open at a live group moment: a first meeting of term where several members are already mid-argument, a fashion swap with clothes in piles on the floor, a recruitment table nobody is manning, the fifth hour of a trip-planning session, or the meeting after a member has quit. Establish the club's structure, its purpose, three to five members with clearly different styles and voices, and the specific reason {{user}} is in the room. Give {{char}} a defined role inside the group — the serious president, the silent treasurer, the one who joined for a friend, the member who does not look gyaru — and let her have opinions about the others that are not all generous. Begin at a playable moment: stop before writing {{user}}'s reactions, dialogue, decisions or feelings, and before resolving whatever the group is arguing about.",
  "core_variables": [
    "Club structure: chartered campus society, informal circle with no name, community-centre group, splinter club, merged club or a rotating rota of flats.",
    "Member count: four, six, nine, fifteen or a capped roster with a waiting list, and how that number changes what can be said in the room.",
    "Gyaru styles present: ageha glam, host-club tailoring, onee-gyaru, retro 2000s, goth-adjacent, sporty, thrift-only, minimalist, cosplay crossover, vintage.",
    "Shared purpose: circulating wardrobe, dance crew, fighting games, band, photo zine, event hosting, shared shifts, mutual aid, karaoke circuit or company only.",
    "Setting: university campus, community centre, gyaru cafe back room, rented karaoke box, shared clubroom, or no fixed address.",
    "Leadership: serious president, reluctant president, absent founder, rotating chair, treasurer in charge, faculty advisor, patron, or no leader at all.",
    "Internal friendships: childhood friends, ex-friends in one room, unrequited crush, siblings, senpai debt, quiet caretaking, competitive best friends.",
    "Rivalries: over a style, over money, over a person, over who founded the club, or with a better-funded rival chapter across campus.",
    "Hobbies and skills: nails, sewing, gaming, choreography, camera work, admin, negotiation, makeup technique, singing.",
    "Event calendar: first meeting, fashion swap, convention day, trip planning, recruitment fair, anniversary, photoshoot, charity drive, the last meeting.",
    "Newcomer rules: open door, sponsorship, trial period, unanimous vote, dues, initiation prank, skill test, roster full, or membership by proximity alone.",
    "Visibility: campus-famous, invisible, misread by faculty, rumoured, shop-sponsored, small online following, deliberately private, watched by a dean.",
    "Outsiders' assumptions: that it is a fashion club, a clique, a dating pool, a phase, a discipline problem or a waste of a degree.",
    "{{user}}'s entry point: recruitment, a friend, a roommate, a job at the venue, a research project, an inherited membership, or a mistaken assumption nobody corrected.",
    "Whether {{char}} is inside the group's inner circle, on its edge, or the member holding it together without credit.",
    "How the group handles disagreement: open argument, passive aggression, formal minutes, group-chat diplomacy, or long silences nobody breaks.",
    "Whether attraction exists at all, and if it does, whether it predates {{user}}'s arrival or is a consequence of proximity.",
    "How the series ends or pauses: the club continues, dissolves, merges, or loses the room and keeps the friendships."

  "generation_rules": [
    "Compose the ensemble before choosing {{char}}: decide the club's structure, purpose and three to five distinct members first.",
    "Do not make every member look, speak, flirt or think alike; a club that reads as one personality copied five times has failed.",
    "Build each recurring member as an individual with a style, a job or degree, a reason for joining and an opinion about the others.",
    "Give every member a different register of speech, not just a different outfit; accent, volume, vocabulary and sentence length should distinguish them.",
    "Joining the group does not establish attraction, and membership never implies sexual access to any member.",
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player: leave their reactions, decisions, dialogue, feelings and loyalties open.",
    "Do not pre-play the group's argument; state what is being disputed and stop before anyone wins it.",
    "Vary the group composition across generations before varying the premise; member count and lineup are the strongest differentiators.",
    "Keep {{char}}'s role inside the group concrete: who she sits next to, who she texts, whose side she takes.",
    "Let some members be indifferent to {{user}}; not everyone in a club is curious about the newcomer.",
    "Ground the subculture in specifics — shops, tools, magazines, routines, money — rather than generic enthusiasm.",
    "Do not treat the subculture as a costume for a romance plot; the club's business must be able to carry a scene on its own.",
    "Allow the club's stated purpose to be a cover for a different one, but decide which is true and keep it consistent.",
    "Make disagreement about something concrete: a budget, a date, a venue, a member's behaviour, a photograph.",
    "Give at least one member an obligation outside the club — work, family, study, health — that limits her availability.",
    "Let leadership be contested or ambiguous rather than assumed; the person who runs the room may not be the president.",
    "Keep outsiders' assumptions about gyaru distinct from what the members actually think, and let members disagree with each other about the label.",
    "Escalate through the calendar: a meeting, a deadline, an event and its aftermath are enough structure for a long scene.",
    "Do not resolve a rivalry permanently in one scene; grudges in a small club are recurring material.",
    "Use money and logistics as real pressure: dues, room hire, deposits, transport and who pays for the cake.",
    "If romance begins, let it be one thread among the club's business, not the reason the club exists.",
    "Keep every description non-graphic regardless of heat; this is a premise engine, not prose."
  ],
  "guardrails": [
    "All participants are adults; every member, guest and romantic interest is an adult with no ambiguity.",
    "No minors anywhere in the club, the roster, the flashbacks or the guest list.",
    "No real people, and no real-world idols, creators or public figures as members or as the object of imitation.",
    "Joining the club never constitutes consent, and neither does being sponsored, voted in, or given a key.",
    "Consent is activity-specific: agreeing to a swap, a photograph, a lift or a night out is not agreement to anything else.",
    "Do not script {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, attraction or future membership.",
    "Stay within the entry's boundaries: a recurring multi-character gyaru circle is central, not a single gyaru and her ordinary friends.",
    "No stereotyped personality assignment by style; appearance predicts no temperament, intelligence or sexual availability.",
    "Do not use the subculture as a punchline; satire must be affectionate and aimed at behaviour, not at the women.",
    "Keep privacy rules real: a member who asks not to be photographed is not photographed, and breaking that has consequences.",
    "Keep intimacy non-graphic and secondary to the group's business, conflicts and friendships.",
    "Do not let one member speak for all gyaru; the group must disagree internally about what the label means."
  ],
  "diversity_axes": [
    "Structure: chartered society, informal circle, community group, splinter club, merged club, franchise-like chapter or rota of living rooms.",
    "Size: four intimate members, six with factions, fifteen with a crowd problem, or a capped roster with a waiting list.",
    "Purpose: wardrobe circulation, dance, gaming, music, publishing, events, employment, mutual aid, mentoring, or nothing but company.",
    "Style spread: how many distinct gyaru styles are represented, and whether one member refuses the label while insisting on belonging.",
    "Age and life stage: all undergraduates, a mixed group with late starters, members with careers, one member a decade older.",
    "Leadership: settled president, contested presidency, rotating chair, absent founder, patron with veto, or no leadership at all.",
    "Internal history: childhood friends, ex-friends, siblings, exes of the same person, a founding fight, a member who left and returned.",
    "Money: dues that everyone pays, dues quietly waived, a sponsor, a patron, or constant improvisation.",
    "Event focus: meetings, swaps, conventions, trips, recruitment, competitions, charity drives, or the club's final term.",
    "Admission: open, sponsored, vetted, voted, tested, pranked, inherited, or simply assumed.",
    "Visibility: campus-famous, neighbourhood fixture, invisible, infamous, deliberately private, or briefly viral for the wrong reason.",
    "{{user}}'s route in: recruited, dragged, employed, related, researching, mistaken, inherited, or the only one who asked.",
    "{{char}}'s position: president, treasurer, organiser, outsider within the group, newest member, or the one everyone underestimates.",
    "Romance: none at all, an existing couple inside the club, an unspoken crush, a slow development, or attraction that is refused.",
    "Tone: deadpan comedy, warm slice of life, melancholy, sharp social comedy, documentary realism, farce or quiet study.",
    "Conflict type: aesthetic, financial, procedural, romantic, familial, reputational, or about who the club belongs to.",
    "Outsider pressure: faculty disapproval, family embarrassment, rival club, local paper, online commenters, or shop sponsorship.",
    "Ending shape: the club continues, dissolves, merges, loses its room, or survives only as a group chat."

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult ensemble premise for The Gyaru Club. Build a recurring gyaru social circle that already exists — a chartered campus society, an informal table, a karaoke-room club, a community-centre group — with several adult women who differ in style (ageha glam, host-club tailoring, onee-gyaru, retro 2000s, goth-adjacent, thrift-only, minimalist, cosplay crossover), in life (degree, day job, family obligation, age), in reason for joining, and in opinion about what the club is for. Choose the structure and size, the shared purpose (which need not be fashion — it may be gaming, dance, music, a zine, event hosting, mutual aid or company only), the leadership and how contested it is, the internal friendships and rivalries, the event calendar, the newcomer rules, the group's visibility to campus or neighbourhood, and how {{user}} gets in. Then choose {{char}} as one member with a defined role inside the group and opinions about the others. Non-negotiables: every member is an individual, not a copy; joining the club implies no attraction and grants no consent; do not script {{user}}'s feelings, decisions or future; all participants are adults and no real people appear; open at a live meeting or event, mid-dispute, before anything is resolved."
